name: Messenger M2 prep — consolidate Messenger vs Teams (decision document)
description:
1. Scope: reviewed which chat surface (Messenger vs Teams) should be the foundation for the messenger epic (channels, membership, external users) — read-only, no app code changed.
2. Discovery: the real Teams UI is `client/src/views/TeamView.vue` + `client/src/components/team-view/*` (no `components/teams/*`), and it is a roster screen that never renders `ChatView`.
3. Contract drift verified with file:line refs — backend routes teams by `name` and exposes no `/members` route, `Team` has no `id`/`users`/`profiles`, and the client addresses teams by UUID and posts `{ profiles, users }` to `/api/teams/{uuid}/members`.
4. Conclusion: Teams membership is broken today (404 route, `undefined` identity, dropped payload, broken read path), and per-channel identity, visibility and guest roles do not exist anywhere.
5. Output: wrote `docs/messenger/implementation-review.md` comparing Options A/B/C with effort ranges and recommending Option A — Messenger canonical, Teams reduced to roster/profile configuration.

Objective: one written decision document that explains the TWO chat surfaces that exist today, states exactly where they disagree with the backend, and proposes the consolidation option management must pick before M2 work starts. No refactor in this task.

Why this profile: `analyst` produces the well-defined, evidence-based document the decision needs; `project` checks the proposal against the project's real architecture/tech stack so we do not propose a second chat stack.

Evidence already gathered (verify, extend, correct):
1. Two parallel implementations of the same idea:
   - Messenger: `client/src/views/MessengerView.vue` + `client/src/components/messenger/*`; channels are chats with `mode === 'channel'`, board `messenger`; list comes from the `channels` getter in `client/src/store/chats.js`.
   - Teams: `client/src/store/teams.js` + `client/src/components/teams/*`; creates chats with `board: team:<id>`, own categories, members, DMs.
2. The Teams client does not match the Teams backend:
   - backend `api/codx/junior/api/teams.py` routes by TEAM NAME (`PUT/DELETE /api/teams/{team_name}`), has no `/members` sub-resource, and `api/codx/junior/model/team.py` `Team` has NO `users` field (a team is a roster of PROFILES, not of people).
   - client `client/src/api/modules/teams.js` calls `POST /api/teams/{id}/members` and `DELETE /api/teams/{id}/members` with `{ profiles, users }`, and addresses teams by uuid `id`.
   - conclusion to confirm: add/remove member and user-membership in Teams currently cannot work against this API.

Steps:
1. Write `docs/messenger/implementation-review.md` with: (a) what exists today per surface (table), (b) the contract mismatches above with file:line references, (c) which surface should be canonical for "team chat", (d) what has to change to have ONE membership model (users + profiles per channel), (e) effort ranges (optimistic/likely/pessimistic) for each option.
2. Give 3 options with a recommendation, e.g.: A) Messenger becomes canonical, Teams becomes roster/membership config only; B) Teams becomes canonical and Messenger is absorbed; C) both stay, Messenger = quick chat, Teams = workspace.
3. List what is required for "external user" access (a channel visible to someone outside the workspace) — what identity/permission concept is missing today (channel membership list, per-channel visibility, guest role).

Acceptance: the document answers "which chat surface do we build on" with a recommendation, names the required API changes, and gives a cost range per option. No code changed.

Target: D+3.

Conclusion: is Teams membership functional today yes/no.
3. Three options (A: Messenger canonical, Teams = roster config only — recommended; B: Teams canonical, Messenger absorbed; C: both stay) each with: what changes, effort range (optimistic / likely / pessimistic), and what breaks.
4. What is missing for the "external user" criterion: the identity / per-channel visibility / guest-role concept that does not exist today, per channel.
5. One short paragraph on the two profiles' view (from `project`) on whether option A fits the existing architecture.

Acceptance: the file exists, answers "which surface" with a recommendation, names the required API changes, and gives a cost range per option. No application code changed.

I'll write the decision document. # Messenger vs Teams — implementation review (Decision D1) - **Status:** Draft for decision **D1** - **Due:** Wed, Nov 4 - **Scope:** read-only review. No application code changed by this document. - **Question:** which chat surface do we build on? ## Objective Decide which existing chat surface is the foundation for the messenger work (channels, membership, external users). The decision has to be made against what is actually in the tree today, not against the intended design. ## Decision at a glance | Question | Answer | |---|---| | Which surface do we build on? | **Messenger** (`client/src/views/MessengerView.vue` + `client/src/views/ChatView.vue`) | | What does Teams become? | **Roster / profile configuration only** (no chat surface) | | Is Teams membership functional today? | **No** — the client contract does not match the server contract (see §2) | | Required API changes | Address teams by **`name`**, send **`members` / `lead`**, and **drop or implement** `/members` (see §3, Option A) | | Are external users supported today? | **No** — identity, per-channel visibility and the guest role do not exist (see §4) | --- ## 1. What exists today, per surface | Dimension | Messenger surface | Teams surface | |---|---|---| | **Entry point** | `client/src/views/MessengerView.vue` | `client/src/views/TeamView.vue`. The task brief says `client/src/components/teams/*`; that directory does not exist in this tree — the actual components are `client/src/components/team-view/*` (`TeamMemberCard.vue`, `TeamMemberDrawer.vue`, `CreateTeamDialog.vue`, `AddMembersToTeamDialog.vue`, `AddTeamMemberDialog.vue`, `ToolDetailsModal.vue`). | | **Chat renderer** | Renders `client/src/views/ChatView.vue` (``) | **None.** `TeamView.vue` is a roster/management screen: grid/board of profiles, drag & drop, skills. It never renders `ChatView`. | | **Channel list** | `client/src/components/messenger/MessengerChannelList.vue` (desktop sidebar + mobile drawer) | None | | **Member / group panel** | `client/src/components/messenger/MessengerGroupInfo.vue` — rendered today in the desktop `
` and the mobile overlay | `TeamMemberCard.vue`, `TeamMemberDrawer.vue`, team dialogs | | **Channel model** | Chats with `mode === 'channel'`, read through the `channels` getter in `client/src/store/chats.js`. `MessengerView.createGroup()` creates `mode: 'channel'`, `board: 'messenger'`. | Would be chats with `board: team:`, `column: categoryId`, `mode: channel.mode` (default `'topic'`). This only exists as actions in `client/src/store/teams.js` (`createChannel`, `openDirectMessage`); **`TeamView.vue` never calls them**. | | **Team identity** | Chat `id` (server UUID) via `$api.chats` | Client-generated `id: crypto.randomUUID()` (`client/src/store/teams.js:12`); every API call addresses `/api/teams/{id}` | | **Membership** | `chat.profiles` (AI profile names) edited by `MessengerGroupInfo` → `$storex.chats.saveChatInfo` | AI: `team.profiles`; humans: `team.members[].username` → `{ profiles, users }` payload | | **Unread** | `countChannelUnread(chat.messages, username)` in `client/src/utils/chatUnread.js:40-43` | None | | **Persistence** | Chats API (`$api.chats`) | Teams API (`$api.teams`) + `localStorage` view state (`client/src/store/teams.js`, `STORAGE_KEY = 'codx-teams-store'`) | | **Status today** | Working chat surface, one store, one renderer | Roster UI that cannot round-trip its membership contract (§2) | Current data flow: ```mermaid flowchart LR subgraph Messenger MV[MessengerView.vue] --> CV[ChatView.vue] MV --> MCL[MessengerChannelList.vue] MV --> MGI[MessengerGroupInfo.vue] MV -->|"$storex.chats.channels
mode === 'channel'"| CS[(chats store)] CS -->|"$api.chats"| CAPI[chats API] end subgraph Teams TV[TeamView.vue] --> TVC["components/team-view/*"] TV -->|"$api.teams / $api.profiles"| TAPI[teams API] TS[(teams store
store/teams.js)] -->|"$api.teams.list"| TAPI TS -.->|"createChannel / openDirectMessage
board: team:<id>"| CS end ``` --- ## 2. Contract mismatches (verified against the tree) ### (a) The backend routes by **team name** and has **no `/members` sub-resource** `api/codx/junior/api/teams.py` registers exactly these routes: | Route | Evidence | |---|---| | `GET /api/teams` | `api/codx/junior/api/teams.py:84` | | `GET /api/teams/{team_name}` | `api/codx/junior/api/teams.py:111` | | `POST /api/teams` | `api/codx/junior/api/teams.py:137` | | `PUT /api/teams/{team_name}` | `api/codx/junior/api/teams.py:170` | | `DELETE /api/teams/{team_name}` | `api/codx/junior/api/teams.py:215` | There is **no** `POST /api/teams/{name}/members` and **no** `DELETE /api/teams/{name}/members`: the module ends at `api/codx/junior/api/teams.py:242` and registers only the five routes above. The file's own contract states that a rename is `POST` + `DELETE` because the folder name must always equal the team name (`api/codx/junior/api/teams.py:22-23`). ### (b) The `Team` model has **no `users`** field `class Team` is declared at `api/codx/junior/model/team.py:200`. Its complete field block is `api/codx/junior/model/team.py:223-276`: - `name`, `description`, `goal`, `avatar` - `lead` (`api/codx/junior/model/team.py:236-239`) - `members: List[TeamMember]` (`api/codx/junior/model/team.py:240-246`) - `tools`, `llm_model`, `use_knowledge`, `tags`, `content`, `path`, `project_id`, `created_at`, `updated_at` There is **no `users`** field. Additional drift the client relies on but the model does not have: **no `id`, no `profiles`, no `color`, no `icon`, no `logo`**. The only membership shape is `members` + `lead`; `profile_names` is derived in `Team.definition()` and never stored. A `TeamMember` (`api/codx/junior/model/team.py:140`) is an AI profile reference (`profile`, `role`, `responsibility`, `order` — `MEMBER_TOOL_FIELDS`, `api/codx/junior/model/team.py:84`), not a human membership. ### (c) The client addresses teams by **UUID** and posts `/members` with `{ profiles, users }` `client/src/api/modules/teams.js`: | Client call | What it sends | Evidence | |---|---|---| | `get(teamId)` | `GET /api/teams/{uuid}` | `client/src/api/modules/teams.js:29-31` | | `update(team)` | `PUT /api/teams/{team.id}` | `client/src/api/modules/teams.js:48-50` | | `delete(teamId)` | `DELETE /api/teams/{uuid}` | `client/src/api/modules/teams.js:57-59` | | `addMembers(teamId, { profiles, users })` | `POST /api/teams/{uuid}/members` with `{ profiles, users }` | `client/src/api/modules/teams.js:69-74` | | `removeMembers(teamId, { profiles, users })` | `DELETE /api/teams/{uuid}/members?profiles=…&users=…` | `client/src/api/modules/teams.js:86-94` | The UUID comes from the local store: `id: crypto.randomUUID()` (`client/src/store/teams.js:12`). `toApiTeam` sends `id`, `profiles` and `users` (`client/src/store/teams.js:74-84`). `client/src/components/team-view/config.js` repeats the pattern: `toLocalTeam` reads `apiTeam.id` / `apiTeam.profiles`, and `toApiTeam` sends `id`, `color`, `icon`, `logo`, `profiles`. `TeamView.vue` consumes that contract in `saveTeam()` (`api.update(apiTeam)`), `deleteTeam()` (`api.delete(team.id)`), `addMembersToTeam()` (`api.addMembers(teamId, { profiles })`) and `removeMemberFromTeam()` (`api.removeMembers(team.id, { profiles })`). ### Conclusion: **is Teams membership functional today? No.** Four independent failures stack up: 1. **Route 404.** `POST/DELETE /api/teams/{id}/members` matches no backend route (`api/codx/junior/api/teams.py:84-242`). 2. **Identity 404.** `team.id` is `undefined`, because `Team.definition()` returns `model_dump()` + `profile_names` and the model has no `id` (`api/codx/junior/model/team.py:200, 223-276`). The client therefore calls `PUT /api/teams/undefined`, `DELETE /api/teams/undefined` and `POST /api/teams/undefined/members`. 3. **Payload dropped.** Even through the working `PUT /api/teams/{name}`, the client sends `profiles` / `users` / `color` / `icon` / `logo`. `Team` does not declare those fields and has no `model_config` overriding `extra`, so they are ignored. The server expects `members` / `lead`; the AI roster and the human users never persist. 4. **Read path broken too.** `toLocalTeam` reads `apiTeam.profiles`, but the server returns `members` + `profile_names`. Every team therefore maps to `profiles: []`; `memberTeamIds()` returns `[]` for every profile and the entire roster falls into the derived "Unassigned" group. ```mermaid sequenceDiagram participant UI as TeamView.vue participant API as api/modules/teams.js participant BE as api/teams.py UI->>API: addMembers(team.id, { profiles }) Note over API: team.id is undefined
(Team model has no id) API->>BE: POST /api/teams/undefined/members BE-->>API: 404 Not Found API-->>UI: error — roster unchanged ``` --- ## 3. Options Effort is in **dev-days** for one senior developer familiar with the repo, including tests/manual QA and excluding design and the external-user work (§4, a separate epic). Treat the ranges as ±1 day of slack on the "likely" value. | Option | What it is | Optimistic | Likely | Pessimistic | |---|---|---|---|---| | **A** | Messenger canonical; Teams = roster config only | 2 | 4 | 7 | | **B** | Teams canonical; Messenger absorbed | 10 | 20 | 35 | | **C** | Both surfaces stay | 4 | 8 | 15 | ### Option A — Messenger canonical, Teams = roster/config only (**recommended**) **What changes** - Keep `MessengerView` + `ChatView` as the only chat UI. Channels remain `mode === 'channel'` chats on `board: 'messenger'`. - `client/src/api/modules/teams.js`: address teams by `name` (`PUT/DELETE /api/teams/{name}`); remove `addMembers` / `removeMembers` (or route them through the existing `PUT` with the full roster); stop sending `users`, `profiles`, `color`, `icon`, `logo`. - `client/src/components/team-view/config.js`: map `name` as identity, `avatar`, `members` / `lead` / `profile_names`; keep `color` / `icon` / `logo` as local-only view state. - `client/src/views/TeamView.vue`: re-key chips, board columns and drag & drop from `t.id` to `name` (`selectedTeamIds`, `memberTeamIds`, `boardColumns`, `:key`s). - `client/src/store/teams.js`: remove (or quarantine) the channel/DM chat actions `createChannel` / `openDirectMessage`, which produce `board: team:` chats that no surface renders today. **What breaks** - Every `TeamView` reference to `t.id` needs rekeying; until then chips, columns and drag & drop collapse (all ids are `undefined`). - `store/teams.js` `createChannel` / `openDirectMessage` become dead code. Any chat already written with `board: team:` is orphaned — note these use `mode: channel.mode` (default `'topic'`), so they are **not** in Messenger's `mode === 'channel'` list either. - `color` / `icon` / `logo` are client-only and are lost on reload unless persisted in the localStorage view state. - External users remain unsupported (unchanged by this option). ### Option B — Teams canonical, Messenger absorbed **What changes** - Make Teams the chat surface: add a stable `id` and `users` / roles to the backend `Team` (`api/codx/junior/model/team.py`), add `POST/DELETE /api/teams/{name}/members` (`api/codx/junior/api/teams.py`), and migrate channels to `board: team:`. - Port the Messenger experience into `components/team-view/*`: channel list, group info, unread, mobile drawer and bottom nav. - Migrate existing `mode === 'channel'` / `board: 'messenger'` chats, and resolve the folder-name-equals-team-name invariant before introducing a UUID. **What breaks** - Existing Messenger channels disappear from the new surface unless migrated. - The `name == folder` invariant (`api/codx/junior/api/teams.py:22-23`) conflicts with UUID identity; migration of `.codx/teams//` is required and risks data loss. - Every `GET /api/teams` consumer (including `TeamView`) must adopt the new shape. - Re-implements unread, group management and mobile navigation that already work in Messenger. ### Option C — Both stay **What changes** - Keep both chat surfaces and patch the Teams contract enough to work (this is Option A plus a second chat surface). - Duplicate unread, group-management and membership fixes on both sides. **What breaks** - Two identity models (chat UUID vs team UUID/name) and two chat entry points; data and unread semantics diverge. - Every fix lands twice; "keep both" still requires the Option A contract fixes on the Teams side. - Users get two places to start a conversation, with no rule about which one owns a channel. --- ## 4. What is missing for the "external user" criterion Today the only human identity is the project session user (`$user` / `$storex.users`). Messages carry `user` and `read_by` (`client/src/utils/chatUnread.js:23-27`), which is **read tracking, not access control**. `$storex.chats.channels` returns **every** `mode === 'channel'` chat and `MessengerView` renders all of them to anyone who can open the project. There is no `visibility` flag, no per-channel membership list and no guest role. `TeamMember` is an AI profile reference (`api/codx/junior/model/team.py:140`, fields `profile` / `role` / `responsibility` / `order` — `api/codx/junior/model/team.py:84`); `Team` has no `users` (`api/codx/junior/model/team.py:223-276`). The `role: 'member'` default in `createMember()` (`client/src/store/teams.js`) is view-only and is never persisted, because the backend stores no human membership. Per channel, the following does not exist anywhere in the tree: | Concept | Today | Per-channel requirement | Where it belongs | |---|---|---|---| | **Identity** | Project session user; `message.user` / `message.read_by` | A membership principal per channel (user id/email) | Chat model or a new `ChannelMember` record | | **Per-channel visibility** | Every channel is returned to every project user | `visibility: 'public' \| 'private'` + an ACL filter in the channel query | `Chat` model + chats API + `MessengerView.channels` | | **Guest role** | No human role; only the AI `TeamMember.role` | `member` / `guest` capability set (tools, write, invite) enforced server-side | Membership record + tool policy | | **Read state** | `read_by` per message | Unread per member, gated by ACL | Keep `read_by`, filter by visibility | ```mermaid flowchart TD U[External user] -->|needs| I[Identity per channel] U -->|needs| V[Visibility public/private] U -->|needs| R[Role: member / guest] I --> M[(Channel membership)] V --> M R --> M M --> API[Chats API ACL] API --> MV[MessengerView channels] ``` --- ## 5. Profiles' view: does Option A fit the existing architecture? From the `project` context, the **Vue Developer** view is that Option A fits because the client already has one chat engine (`ChatView`) driven by one store (`$storex.chats`), and Messenger is the only surface wired to it; `TeamView.vue` talks directly to `$project.$api.teams` / `$project.$api.profiles` and never renders a conversation, so making Teams canonical would mean building a second chat surface and a schema migration. The **analyst** view reaches the same conclusion from the contract side: Option A is the smallest and most reversible diff, it corrects the Teams contract (name identity, `members`/`lead`, no `/members`) without touching the working chat path, and it keeps a single documented source of truth for channels. Both profiles therefore support Option A. --- ## Required API changes (Option A) - [ ] `client/src/api/modules/teams.js`: replace `{teamId}` with `{team_name}` in `get` / `update` / `delete`; **remove** `addMembers` / `removeMembers` (no backend route) or reimplement them on top of `PUT /api/teams/{team_name}` with the full roster. - [ ] `client/src/api/modules/teams.js`: send `{ name, description, avatar, members, lead, tools, llm_model, use_knowledge, tags, content }` — **no** `id`, `users`, `profiles`, `color`, `icon`, `logo`. - [ ] `client/src/components/team-view/config.js`: `toLocalTeam` / `toApiTeam` map `name` as identity, `avatar`, `members` / `lead` / `profile_names`; keep view-only fields local. - [ ] `client/src/views/TeamView.vue`: rekey chips, columns and drag & drop from `id` to `name`; update `saveTeam()` / `deleteTeam()` / `addMembersToTeam()` / `removeMemberFromTeam()` accordingly. - [ ] `client/src/store/teams.js`: drop or quarantine `createChannel` / `openDirectMessage` (they write `board: team:` chats no surface renders); stop emitting `users` / `profiles` in `toApiTeam`. - [ ] **Backend, only if partial updates are required:** add `POST/DELETE /api/teams/{team_name}/members` in `api/codx/junior/api/teams.py`, delegating to `Team.upsert_member` / `Team.remove_member` (`api/codx/junior/model/team.py`) and returning `definition(include_content=True)`.     .codx/teams/<Name>/<Name>.md     # Markdown charter (team instructions)

folder-name-equals-name invariant, so the mental model is the same.
